tables.title: Source datasets
tables.description: Every upstream dataset DataNepal draws on, with publisher, URL, licence, retrieval date, and whether the publisher revises previously published values.

tables.title: Dimension members
tables.description: The permitted values for each dimension, with bilingual labels and an optional parent for hierarchical dimensions such as budget categories. An observation may only use members declared here, which is what keeps extensible dimensions from becoming a free-text field.

tables.title: Dimensions
tables.description: The dimensions observations can be broken down by — sex and age band today, and whatever future datasets require. Adding a dataset adds rows here rather than columns to the fact table.

tables.title: Nepal administrative geography
tables.description: Convenience view of the 753 local units with their district and province lineage denormalised onto each row, for consumers who want one flat file rather than walking the parent chain in places.
attribution: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
caveats: Excludes protected areas, which are not local units.
Derived from places; places is the canonical table.

tables.title: Indicators
tables.description: What each measured concept means, its default unit, and crucially whether it is additive. Aggregating a non-additive indicator is the most common way to produce a confidently wrong number, so the policy is data rather than documentation.

tables.title: Licences
tables.description: Reuse terms, with share-alike and attribution flags recorded as booleans so licence compatibility can be tested mechanically rather than reasoned about.

tables.title: Observation dimension members
tables.description: Long-format dimension assignments for each observation. Joining this to observations reconstructs the full key of a measurement.
caveats: An observation with no dimensions has no rows here. That is normal for scalar indicators like national inflation.

tables.title: Observations
tables.description: The canonical fact table. One row per measurement: an indicator, optionally a place, a period, a set of dimension members, and a value. Every dataset on the platform lands in this shape, which is what lets one component render any indicator without dataset-specific code.
tables.grain: One row per (dataset, indicator, place, period, dimension combination, revision). Only rows with is_current = true are the present truth.
caveats:
Dimensions are not columns. They live in observation_dimensions, keyed by dimension_key, so a new dataset introduces dimension members rather than schema changes.
Totals coexist with their components -- population has sex='all' alongside 'female' and 'male'. Filter by dimension_key or dimension members; never sum blindly.
Check the indicator's is_additive flag before aggregating. Rates and ratios (inflation, GDP per capita, density) must not be summed or unweighted-averaged.
A NULL value with status 'suppressed' or 'not_collected' is meaningful and distinct from zero.

tables.title: Source registry
tables.description: Every organisation DataNepal cites — as a publisher, an acquisition source, or both — with its Nepali name, type, jurisdiction, and provenance tier.
caveats:
source_tier records provenance authority, not data quality. A Tier A ministry publishing a badly-formatted PDF is more authoritative than a Tier C aggregator's clean CSV of the same numbers.
The National Statistics Office was called the Central Bureau of Statistics until 2022. Aggregator records still use the old name; both resolve to nso.

tables.title: Nepal boundary geometry
tables.description: Simplified administrative boundary geometry for Nepal at all three admin levels -- 7 provinces, 77 districts, and 775 local units and protected areas -- as GeoJSON MultiPolygon strings in lon/lat, joined to canonical place identifiers.
tables.grain: One row per place with geometry.
attribution: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
caveats:
Simplified with Ramer-Douglas-Peucker, at a tolerance chosen per admin level because each is drawn at a different scale: 0.004 degrees for provinces, 0.006 for districts, and 0.0015 for local units, which are drawn a district at a time and so occupy far more of the frame. Across the three levels this reduces about 1.4 million vertices to roughly 63,000. Fine for cartographic display at web sizes; not suitable for area calculation, adjacency analysis, or any measurement. Use the source package for that.
Rings under roughly 1 km² are dropped, so small river islands and slivers are absent.
Because each level is simplified independently, a border shared between two levels carries different vertices at each one. Province, district and local boundaries are therefore not exactly coincident and should not be overlaid on one another expecting them to line up.
Level 3 contains 775 features: the 753 local units plus 22 protected areas. Protected areas are federally administered and are not local government units. The distinction is carried by the P-code type digit, never by name.
Coordinates are lon/lat (EPSG:4326). No projection is applied.

tables.title: Place identifiers by source system
tables.description: Maps external identifiers to DataNepal place_ids. This is the crosswalk layer that lets a source keyed on its own codes join the canonical geography without name matching.
tables.grain: One row per (place, identifier system, identifier value).
attribution: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
caveats: Identifier values are unique within their system, not globally. Always qualify a lookup by id_system.

tables.title: Nepal places
tables.description: Every place DataNepal can attach an observation to, across all types: country, provinces, districts, local units, and later wards, electoral constituencies, and protected areas. Keyed by a stable internal place_id with explicit parent relationships.
attribution: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
caveats:
place_id is a DataNepal surrogate, not a source code. Source identifiers (OCHA P-codes, Wikidata QIDs) live in place_identifiers so a place survives a source renumbering its codes.
Parent relationships are explicit foreign keys, not derived from P-code substrings. Substring nesting works for the administrative hierarchy and breaks for constituencies and protected areas.
Nepali names cover provinces (hand-verified) and ~66% of local units (Wikidata). Districts have none yet. NULL means no verified name exists; names are never transliterated.

tables.title: Nepal protected areas
tables.description: National parks, wildlife reserves, hunting reserves, and conservation areas. Federally administered and outside local-unit jurisdiction, so kept out of the administrative hierarchy.
tables.grain: One row per protected area and district it intersects.
attribution: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
caveats: Several protected areas span districts and therefore appear more than once.
Identified by P-code type digit 5, which depends on OCHA's coding convention.

tables.title: Table-to-source links
tables.description: Which source datasets each published table draws on. This is what makes the effective licence of a table computable rather than asserted.
tables.grain: One row per (published table, source dataset).

tables.title: Topics
tables.description: The browse dimension: subject areas users navigate by, with counts of how much data each currently holds.
caveats: status = 'planned' means DataNepal intends to cover the topic and holds no data for it yet. The site must not present a planned topic as populated.

tables.title: Units of measure
tables.description: Units, including currency and price basis. Currency and price basis are part of the unit rather than separate columns, so 'US dollars, current prices' and 'US dollars, constant 2015 prices' are distinct and never silently compared.

history.title: Observation revision history
history.description: Append-only history of every published observation. One row per revision; is_current marks the present value. A superseded row keeps its original value and records when it was replaced.

sources.title: Nepal — Subnational Administrative Boundaries
sources.publisher: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
caveats: P-codes are OCHA identifiers, not a Nepali government standard. They are recorded as source identifiers against canonical places rather than used as canonical identity.
Models 775 units at admin level 3, of which 22 are protected areas rather than local units. Excluding them gives Nepal's official 753.
English names only; the source publishes no Nepali names.
Published by OCHA Field Information Services Section; DataNepal obtained this copy via the hdx platform. Attribute the publisher, not the platform.

sources.title: Nepal — Subnational Population Statistics
caveats: Figures for 2023 are projections, not census counts. Nepal's most recent census was 2021 (29,164,578). Never present projections as census results.
Coverage stops at district level; there is no local-unit breakdown.
The open-ended top age band is spelled '80Plus' in current files and '80PL' in others. Ingestion accepts both and asserts the measure count per place.
Published by UNFPA; DataNepal obtained this copy via the hdx platform. Attribute the publisher, not the platform.

sources.title: Nepal — National Population and Housing Census 2021
caveats:
NSO states "Copyright © National Statistics Office 2023. All rights reserved." and publishes no open-licence grant. Recording this as reusable with attribution is a deliberate DataNepal decision, not a term NSO has offered: these are official state statistics published for public use, only aggregates are republished, and every figure names NSO and links to source. Anyone relying on these figures commercially should confirm terms with NSO.
Each district carries an INSTITUTIONAL row for population not resident in a household — barracks, hostels, prisons, hospitals. It is 239,098 people nationally and belongs to no local government. Local-unit figures therefore sum to 28,925,480, not to the national 29,164,578; the difference is carried as residence_type = institutional at district level so the hierarchy still reconciles.
The census tables carry no P-codes. Local units are matched to the spine on district, base name and unit type, which resolves 751 of 753 directly with no type disagreements. The remaining two are corrected by an explicit, committed crosswalk (transform/seeds/nso_name_fixes.csv) rather than by fuzzy name matching.
Literacy figures cover the population aged 5 and over, not the whole population. Rates computed against total population would understate literacy everywhere by the size of the under-five cohort.
NSO spells the sub-metropolitan and metropolitan suffixes "Metropolitian" throughout these files. Ingestion accepts both spellings.
This is the 2021 census, an enumeration rather than a projection. It must never be presented interchangeably with the UNFPA 2023 projections also published here.

sources.title: Wikidata — Nepal local units
caveats:
Chosen over OpenStreetMap on licensing grounds, not coverage. OSM carries Nepali names for ~55% of units but is ODbL, whose share-alike terms would propagate to every table this fed.
Covers ~66% of local units. Typing is inconsistent: metropolitan cities are often modelled as the city rather than the administrative unit.
Community-maintained, so names are not authoritative.

sources.title: World Bank World Development Indicators — Nepal
caveats:
The World Bank restates figures as national accounts are revised. The API exposes a lastupdated date per indicator, which is recorded as the publication date of each observation so revisions are traceable.
National level only. These are compiled from Nepali official statistics (largely NRB and the National Statistics Office); the World Bank is the aggregator, not the primary collector.
Inflation and per-capita figures are rates and ratios. They must never be summed or averaged across places or periods without weighting.

notes.licensing: Each table's effective_licence is computed from the sources it draws on, taking the most restrictive. DataNepal does not relicense upstream data; attribution requirements travel with it.
notes.provenance: Every source records both who published the data and where DataNepal obtained this copy. Attribute the publisher, not the platform the copy came from.
notes.additivity: Check the indicators table before aggregating. Rates, ratios, and per-capita measures are marked is_additive = false.
